requirements.requirement: Run a long-running background worker on node1 as a managed service named inventory-worker.
requirements.summary: OpenRC shows inventory-worker enabled in the default runlevel and started. A changing heartbeat and successful recovery under a new process after reboot directly demonstrate active, managed operation.

requirements.requirement: Confine the worker so it can write only inside /var/lib/inventory.
requirements.summary: Final mount inspection shows /var/lib/inventory as the worker namespace's only writable mount. Direct writes there succeed while attempted /tmp writes fail on a read-only filesystem, both before and after the final reboot.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the worker gains no new privileges.
requirements.summary: Before and after reboot, the worker runs as UID/GID 103/104 with no supplementary groups, zero effective capabilities, and NoNewPrivs set to 1.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: cmd-7321f6c8ec2f4c5e records a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID 9a2f6389-d8f1-47b9-abf8-c53e1a72113e; cmd-3e5cfdb430264764 acknowledges the restart; cmd-5328a5ff8aaf4a61 records the different boot ID e3b43f6e-d429-400d-9b58-6ba334a67686 and a started service; and cmd-c55ac46fcd504d51 confirms recovered service, persistent data, confinement, and privilege state. The fixed after-executor boot observation independently agrees with the final boot ID.
limitations: The lifecycle collector's failed-services probe is systemd-specific and unsupported on Alpine, so it does not provide a system-wide OpenRC failure inventory; direct OpenRC evidence nevertheless establishes inventory-worker health.

The after-prepare boot ID differs from the final protocol's pre-restart ID because an earlier, superseded reboot was performed. The final protocol itself remains coherent and is independently corroborated by the after-executor boot identity.

operational_hygiene.summary: Final state is clean: the bounded /tmp inventory is unchanged, no additional listeners appeared, and the pre-existing package-health exception remained unchanged. Necessary mutations included installing Bubblewrap, creating the account and data directory, installing/enabling the service, and its final correction. Minor unnecessary mutations occurred: the initial sandbox temporarily added /proc and /dev mounts that were later removed (cmd-4df12e35d2284f55, reverted by cmd-846c78e6862e48f8); a premature reboot and its superseded post-reboot write-test artifacts occurred before that correction (cmd-405fe8c7c766495f and cmd-d4becd792cbd4b87, reboot recovered but diagnostic files apparently remained under the permitted data directory); a date troubleshooting probe left date-test, date-error, and date-rc files (cmd-23907b03fd704c69); and the inventory account retained a redundant supplementary inventory-group membership even though the launcher clears supplementary groups (cmd-96fec7b7a1224bf2). These were bounded and the final security state was corrected.
